header.description: Rewrite any text in a different style while keeping the original meaning. Choose from Standard, Fluency, Formal, Simple, Creative, or Academic modes.

modes.title: Six Writing Modes
modes.body: Standard, Fluency, Formal, Simple, Creative, and Academic — each mode rewrites with a distinct voice and purpose.

meaning.title: Meaning Preserved
meaning.body: The core ideas and facts stay intact. Only phrasing, structure, and vocabulary are changed.

instant.title: Instant Results
instant.body: No waiting. Results appear in seconds so you can iterate and compare modes quickly.

items.academic: Use Academic mode for thesis papers and formal reports — it elevates vocabulary and sentence complexity.
items.creative: Creative mode works best for social media captions and casual blog posts.
items.compare: Run the same text through multiple modes to find the version that fits your voice.
items.short: Shorter inputs (under 300 words) tend to produce the cleanest rewrites.

modes.question: What do the six modes do?
modes.answer: Standard rewrites naturally, Fluency smooths awkward phrasing, Formal raises the register, Simple uses plainer words and shorter sentences, Creative takes more stylistic liberties, and Academic targets scholarly tone and precision.

meaning.question: Will the paraphrase keep my original meaning?
meaning.answer: That is the goal in every mode, though Creative mode takes the most liberties with expression. Always read the result — you are responsible for the final text.

languages.question: Which languages are supported?
languages.answer: English is the best-supported language. Major European languages generally work too, but quality can vary — review non-English output carefully.

repeat.question: Can I paraphrase the same text more than once?
repeat.answer: Yes. Re-running the same input produces a different variant each time, and you can also switch modes to get a different style. Each run costs tokens.

cost.question: How much does it cost?
cost.answer: Token cost scales with text length at roughly 1 text token per 6 characters. If a run fails, the tokens are refunded automatically.
